results.releaseNotes:
Sort by date, answer a whole review at once, and boards keep their look.

New in this version:
• Sort tasks by newest, oldest or due date
• Reviews show the newest request first
• Long-press or swipe a review request to approve, ask for changes on or reject everything waiting
• Sharing a screenshot to Tasks: choose the board in a panel, with each board's icon and colour
• Boards keep their icon and colour, also when a repository can't be reached for a moment
results.description:
Tasks turns a git repository into task boards. Each card is a markdown file with simple frontmatter, each lane is a folder, and the whole board lives in a repo you own, so you keep full history and your data is portable by default.

Sign in to GitHub with device-flow OAuth, or connect GitHub, GitLab.com or a self-hosted GitLab with a personal access token. There is no hosted service and no separate account: you bring your own git host, and your token is stored in the Keychain.

File a task from a screenshot
• Share a photo or screenshot to Tasks from any app, pick the project, and add it as a new task or to an existing one
• Mark up the image: select a region and comment on it, with quick suggestions
• Tasks drafts a title, description, type and priority from the image and your comments, and you can change all of it
• Use the on-device model on supported iPhones, or your own key for a cloud model
• Your device details are added for bug reports

Work without waiting
• Changes are sent in the background, with an activity view that shows what is still going out
• Create and edit tasks offline; they are sent when you are back online
• See which cards changed since you last looked, and sort by unread, date or priority
• The board list shows how many cards changed on each board

Everything in one place
• All Tasks shows the open tasks of every board you added
• Reviews collects what your boards ask you to approve, with images, audio and video
• Notifications for new reviews and board changes, if you want them
• When a new board appears in a repository you added, Tasks offers to add it

Boards
• View as lanes or a grouped list
• Labels, due dates, comments and an activity log on every task
• Create, edit, move and delete cards, each saved as a commit
• Move a task to another project, keeping or renumbering its id
• Attach images to tasks
• Review assets that a task asks you to approve
• Notes are shown as rendered Markdown, and you edit them right there
• Open a folder or a folder server on your network as a board
• Optional live updates when someone pushes, through a small relay you can host yourself
• Try a demo board first, with no account or connection

Tasks reads and writes the same board format as Tasks for Mac, so a board you edit on one opens on the other. It works over your provider's API, with no local clone required.

For developers and teams who already live in git and want their tasks to travel with the code, in plain files they fully own.

Tasks was called GitKittie Kanban before this version.
